canonical_topic: Two general categories of combustion pollution
definition: Combustion pollution splits into two broad categories: impurities/particles trapped in the fuel that get released when it burns, and greenhouse gases, which are an intrinsic, unavoidable byproduct of the combustion chemistry itself.
core_idea: The author frames fuel-borne particulate contamination and intrinsic greenhouse-gas production as the two fundamentally different types of pollution from burning fossil fuels — one is a fuel-purity issue, the other is unavoidable chemistry.
key_points: First category: impurities or small particles trapped in the fuel, released on combustion.
Second category: greenhouse gases, an intrinsic part of the combustion process itself.
Greenhouse gases are described as not a direct health hazard and generally safe in themselves, but capable of altering global climate when released in large quantities.
relationships: Fly ash and soot as particulate pollution
caveats: Assuming greenhouse gases are toxic like other pollutants — the author distinguishes them as non-hazardous to health individually, with the risk being climate-scale accumulation.
